newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MMS hunts down royalty underpayments.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MMS hunts down royalty underpayments.

text.p: The U.S. Minerals Management Service, responding to a barrage of criticism from a watchdog group, said it had launched a nationwide audit this week for potential underpayments of crude oil royalties.

The Interior Department agency, which collects about $4 billion a year in royalties on oil, gas, and minerals produced on federal lands, said it would clamp down on producers who paid royalties based on posted prices for their crude while selling it at a premium to posted prices.
The latest move follows a similar effort announced a month ago to go after royalty underpayments on oil produced on federal land in California.
At the same time, the Interior Department's inspector general is in the process of completing a report reviewing the agency's settlements of old royalty payment disputes.

In a draft done last November and obtained by the non-profit group Project on Government Oversight (POGO), the inspector general said MMS had left too thin a paper trail, failing to explain why it had settled for far less than the agency believed it was due.
